question: In which decade will the 2026 UK Christmas number one have been originally released?

calls.reasoning: Status quo: Wham!'s Last Christmas (1984) won Xmas #1 in 2023 and 2024 and was #2 in 2025 behind Kylie's heavily promoted Amazon-exclusive XMAS (2025). The 2026 chart week (Dec 18-24) is peak Last Christmas streaming. Before 2023, contemporary releases (LadBaby, Ed Sheeran, charity singles) won every year from 2015 to 2022, so a well-run campaign or a huge current hit (any of which would resolve 2020s) is the main threat. Market check: OLBG table (12 Oct 2026) has Wham 1/2 and Sam Fender & Olivia Dean 6/4, but per OLBG bookmakers aren't taking bets yet and the implied probabilities sum to about 260%, so it is weak evidence only. No Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market found. Mariah Carey (1990s) and Brenda Lee (1950s) are perennial runners-up with small tails.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs share the same evidence base (2023-24 Wham! wins, 2025 Kylie win with Wham! #2, no announced 2026 campaign, no real market). Factual disputes: (1) OLBG favourite (Wham! vs Fender/Dean) — the two OLBG pieces contradict and neither is a real book; unresolvable without web, low weight. (2) Announcement date (~19 vs 25 Dec) — Christmas 2026 is a Friday, so the 25 Dec chart is likely; immaterial to the outcome. Remaining disagreement is pure judgment on the Wham! default vs a push/new-release threat; I lean slightly more toward a 2020s push than the runs' midpoint because Amazon/Kylie's 2025 success demonstrates a repeatable model, while keeping Wham! as the favourite.
